questions.prompt: Why must inventory reservation and the month-start shipment job be idempotent in ParcelPilot, and how would you key them?

keyPoints.text: Idempotent means running the operation twice has the same effect as running it once.
keyPoints.quote: An operation is idempotent when running it twice has the same effect as running it once.

keyPoints.text: Both the inventory reservation and month-start batch generation are named as operations that must be idempotent.
keyPoints.quote: Inventory reservation and month-start batch generation should be idempotent.

keyPoints.text: Today a repeated Reserve click subtracts the reservation from stock again.
Reservation is keyed by the billing cycle so a second reserve for June is recognised.
Shipment generation is keyed by subscriber and cycle, the business identity of one box.
The current job mints a fresh random shipment id on every run, so nothing can detect a repeat without such a key.

questions.prompt: How should retries and outgoing messages (emails, warehouse labels) be designed so partial failures do not double-send or lose work?

keyPoints.text: Every retry design starts from the assumption that the previous attempt partly succeeded.
A shipment can be created while the follow-up event is never logged.
keyPoints.quote: A shipment job could create a shipment but fail before logging the event.

keyPoints.text: A local payment retry can race a provider webhook that already recovered the payment.
keyPoints.quote: A payment retry could update local state after Stripe already recovered through webhook.

keyPoints.text: The outbox row is written atomically with the domain change.
keyPoints.quote: write an outbox row in the same transaction as the domain change

keyPoints.text: A separate worker delivers outbox messages, retrying and deduplicating.
keyPoints.quote: then have a worker deliver messages with retry and dedupe

keyPoints.text: Today 'Send dunning' only logs a timeline event; no message is delivered at all.

questions.prompt: Which current side effects become production risks, and how would an operator notice each one breaking?

keyPoints.text: Everything the app does today is in-memory React state, with no network, queue or email.
keyPoints.quote: Current side effects are local state changes.

keyPoints.text: Timeline events vanish on reload and carry no server timestamp.
keyPoints.quote: Not durable, not ordered by server time.

keyPoints.text: Plan and balance changes made in the browser cannot be trusted as money.
Fail/retry handlers could duplicate retries and dunning emails once real.
The guiding operational question is how you would detect the failure.
keyPoints.quote: Ask "how would I know this broke?"

keyPoints.text: Inventory breakage shows up as negative or over-reserved stock.
keyPoints.quote: Inventory: stock goes negative or too many items reserved.

keyPoints.text: Recommendation breakage shows up as an excluded item in the top picks.
keyPoints.quote: Recommendation: excluded item appears in top recommendations.
